title: Forge 5: a multilayer perceptron that learns XOR

wrong.activation_on_logits.py: the activation is also applied to the output layer, so logits are squashed (tanh caps them at 1)
wrong.skips_activation_grad.py: backward multiplies by W.T but forgets the activation derivative of the hidden layer
wrong.act_grad_wrong_layer.py: every layer's activation derivative is taken at the first layer's pre-activation
wrong.ascent_step.py: SGD adds lr * g (gradient ascent) instead of subtracting it
wrong.rebinding_step.py: step rebinds a local name (p = p - lr * g) instead of updating the array in place, so nothing changes
wrong.grad_not_averaged.py: the logit gradient is not divided by the batch size although the loss is a mean
wrong.bias_grad_first_row.py: db uses only the first example's gradient instead of summing over the batch
wrong.stale_input_cache.py: every layer's cached input is the network input X, so dW of deeper layers is wrong
wrong.unstable_softmax.py: no max-subtraction in the loss: logits near 1000 overflow
wrong.relu_grad_tanh_formula.py: ReLU networks use the tanh derivative in backward
wrong.accumulating_grads.py: dW accumulates across calls instead of being recomputed
wrong.zero_init.py: all weights start at zero: every hidden unit is identical and gets the same gradient forever

hints: Forward: for each layer a = act(a @ W + b), except the last, which returns raw logits. Keep two lists: the input of every linear layer, and the pre-activation z of every hidden layer.

Backward starts from d = (softmax(logits) - onehot(y)) / N. Then for layer i from the last down to the first: dW[i] = input[i].T @ d, db[i] = d.sum(axis=0). To move down a layer: d = (d @ W[i].T) * act'(pre[i-1]).
Modules 3 and 4 are exactly these two pieces. If you wrote Linear and the loss there, you are only wiring them together.
step must change the arrays that params() returns, in place: use `p -= lr * g`, never `p = p - lr * g`.
If XOR does not train, run a finite-difference check on one weight first. A wrong gradient is far more likely than a wrong learning rate.
